hint: He stretched his staff over the Red Sea so Israel could cross on dry ground.
explanation: God parted the Red Sea when Moses raised his staff, opening a dry path for Israel to escape Egypt (Exodus 14:21).

hint: A young shepherd who chose five smooth stones from the stream before facing a giant.
explanation: Armed with only a sling, five smooth stones, and faith in the Lord, David defeated the Philistine giant Goliath (1 Samuel 17:40–49).

hint: He kept praying to God even when a royal decree threatened a night with hungry beasts.
explanation: God sent His angel to shut the lions’ mouths and keep Daniel completely safe through the night in the den (Daniel 6:16–22).

hint: A dove returned to his wooden vessel carrying a fresh olive leaf after the great flood.
explanation: Noah built the ark in obedience to God, saw the dove return with an olive leaf, and received the rainbow as God’s covenant sign (Genesis 8:11; 9:13).

hint: His father gave him a richly ornamented robe, and he dreamed of sheaves and eleven stars bowing.
explanation: Jacob gave Joseph an ornate multicolored robe, and God gave him prophetic dreams of wheat sheaves and eleven stars before his rise in Egypt (Genesis 37:3–9).

hint: He fled by ship from his mission to Nineveh and spent three days inside a great sea creature.
explanation: After Jonah fled God’s call to Nineveh, the Lord appointed a great fish to swallow him for three days and three nights (Jonah 1:17).

hint: This prophet was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind as a chariot of fire separated him from his apprentice.
explanation: A chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared beside the Jordan, and Elijah went up to heaven in a whirlwind while Elisha watched (2 Kings 2:11).

hint: A Nazirite judge whose supernatural strength returned one last time between two temple columns.
explanation: Calling on the Lord for strength one final time, Samson pushed against the two central temple pillars and brought the Philistine house down (Judges 16:29–30).

hint: A courageous queen who approached the Persian throne uninvited and saw the king extend his golden scepter.
explanation: Queen Esther risked her life to enter the king’s court unannounced, and King Xerxes extended his golden scepter to spare her and hear her plea for her people (Esther 5:2).

hint: A short chief tax collector in Jericho who climbed a sycamore-fig tree just to see Jesus pass by.
explanation: Too short to see over the crowd in Jericho, Zacchaeus climbed a sycamore-fig tree where Jesus called him down and invited Himself to his house (Luke 19:4).

hint: With just 300 men, he routed Midian at night using trumpets, empty clay jars, and hidden torches.
explanation: At Gideon’s signal, his 300 men blew their trumpets, smashed their clay jars, and held up blazing torches, throwing the Midianite camp into panic (Judges 7:20).

hint: A loyal Moabite widow who gleaned leftover barley in the fields of Boaz to care for her mother-in-law.
explanation: Out of steadfast devotion to Naomi, Ruth worked faithfully gleaning grain in Boaz’s barley fields in Bethlehem (Ruth 2:2–7).

hint: He led Israel around Jericho for seven days until the priests’ ram’s horns sounded and the walls fell flat.
explanation: Following God’s command under Joshua’s leadership, the priests blew seven ram’s horns, the people shouted, and Jericho’s walls collapsed (Joshua 6:20).

hint: This bold fisherman climbed out of the boat on the Sea of Galilee to walk on the waves toward Jesus.
explanation: When Jesus said 'Come,' Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water toward Him on the Sea of Galilee (Matthew 14:29).

hint: God brought this patriarch outside his tent at night and promised descendants as numerous as the stars.
explanation: God led Abraham outside to gaze at the starry night sky and promised his offspring would be as countless as the stars, and Abraham believed the Lord (Genesis 15:5).
